headline: Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki out 2-4 weeks with upper-body injury, ending ironman streak
take:
The Athletic reports that Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki will be out 2-4 weeks with an upper-body injury, ending his ironman streak at 546 games, the second-longest active streak in the NHL. The Hockey News says the injury underlines Montreal's need to upgrade at center.

The numbers show why this hurts. So far this season, Suzuki has 12 points in 9 games and plays 21.78 minutes a night. He has scored 1.06 goals more than his expected goals (a measure of chance quality) of 3.94, so some of that production is running hot. Still, when he is on the ice at five-on-five, MTL controls 56.97% of the expected goals, and the team's share rises 5.71 percentage points with him out there. MTL's overall share is just 49.2%, with a 4-3-2 record, so he is propping up a team that is otherwise average at best.

With no games missed yet, this is a projection based on how the coach has used his players. Cole Caufield, at 19:26 a night, is next in line for Suzuki's minutes, and Oliver Kapanen, the busiest man on the second power-play unit, is the likeliest to move up to the first unit.
